questions: If there are fewer than 30 unique strings generated, should the histogram show all available strings (less than 30 bars) or should it still show 30 bars with zero frequencies for the missing ones?
Should the top 30 be selected based on frequency count alone, and if ties occur, how should they be broken (e.g., alphabetical order, random, first encountered)?
Is the random string generation with replacement (i.e., each string is independent, so duplicates can occur) or without replacement (ensuring uniqueness until exhaustion)?
Should the histogram bars be ordered by frequency (descending) or by another criterion (e.g., alphabetical order of strings)?
What should happen if n_rows is exactly 1? The function would generate one string, but the histogram of top 30 might be ambiguous.
Are the strings generated uniformly over all possible 3-letter lowercase combinations (26^3 possibilities), or is there any bias (e.g., using random.choices with equal weights)?
Should the function set a specific random seed for reproducibility, or leave it to the caller?
Is the histogram expected to have specific visual styling (e.g., bar colors, grid lines, figure size) beyond the title and axis labels mentioned?
